prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: side impact at intersection in Houston, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1133; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling northbound in the left lane of a signalized intersection in Houston, Texas, when the vehicle was struck on its driver side by Driver 2, who was traveling eastbound and entered the intersection as the signal turned. Driver 1 reported neck pain consistent with whiplash following the impact and was evaluated at the scene. The Passenger in Driver 1's vehicle did not report injury. Two independent witnesses, both standing on the northwest corner, stated that the collision occurred as described by Driver 1 and Driver 2. Scene photographs were taken and show damage concentrated along the driver-side door and quarter panel, which is generally in keeping with the angle and force of a side impact of this type. Driver 2 acknowledged entering the intersection and did not dispute the sequence of events. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy. No prior damage to the vehicle was observed or reported. Officers were unable to fully confirm the seating position Driver 1 occupied at the moment of impact, as the account given at the scene was not entirely precise on that point. Report prepared for the file.
